author: human
request:
Feature request: filter the vet list by specialty. Three product decisions
come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of
  scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in.
  Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The JSON endpoint at /vets is reinstated as a supported surface — this
  filter is its first requested capability. Mint a fresh requirement for it;
  the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused.
- The filter is a URL contract only. Neither surface gains a form, dropdown,
  or other page control in this request; pagination links carry the
  parameter so filtered pages stay navigable. A visible control may come as
  a follow-up request.

Both vet list surfaces accept an optional `specialty` query parameter:

- /vets.html?specialty=<name> — the HTML page shows only vets holding that
  specialty; pagination applies to the filtered list.
- /vets?specialty=<name> — the JSON endpoint returns only those vets.

Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive — not a prefix. A
specialty matching no vet yields the normal page or JSON document with an
empty vet list (HTTP 200). An empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if
the parameter were absent, like the empty owner search. Without the parameter
both endpoints behave as today. Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Narrowing the veterinarian directory to one named specialty
summary: Either published veterinarian list can be narrowed to the veterinarians holding one named specialty, named in the request rather than chosen on the page. The name matches whole and ignores letter case; naming nothing lists everyone.
acceptance_criteria: Both vet list surfaces accept an optional `specialty` request parameter; without it each behaves exactly as it does today.
Naming a specialty narrows either surface to only the veterinarians holding that specialty.
The specialty name is matched whole and ignoring letter case; the opening letters of a name alone match no veterinarian.
A specialty no veterinarian holds yields a successful response with an empty veterinarian list on either surface.
An empty or whitespace-only specialty value behaves as if none were named, and every veterinarian is listed.
Leading or trailing spaces around a specialty name are disregarded, as in an owner search.
On the paged surface the page count reflects the narrowed list, and the page links carry the named specialty so a narrowed page stays navigable.
A veterinarian holding several specialties is listed under each one of them.
Without any named specialty the machine-readable list returns every veterinarian with the specialties each holds.
non_goals: no form, dropdown, or other page control for choosing a specialty
no free-text search for a veterinarian, a pet, or a visit
no narrowing by more than one specialty at once
no paging of the machine-readable list
no revival of the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 id
notes: Autofix audit: no prd-autofix records in the log; nothing to judge. NG-9 narrowed and the machine-readable surface reinstated per the intake decisions, recorded in docs/adr/2026-09-06-non-goal-veterinarian-search.md. The ADR index row in docs/adr/README.md is outside this agent's write scope and still needs adding. Three open questions were recorded in the PRD rather than consulted: a visible control, narrowing by several specialties, and paging the machine-readable list.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The narrowing stays inside the vet feature package and adds no type, no module, and no dependency. Both surfaces keep the Web controller shape: bind the request, delegate, select the response. The matching itself belongs in VetRepository as two specialty-filtered reads — one paged for the HTML surface, one collection for the machine-readable surface — following the Repository row of architecture-principles Pattern Catalog and the derived-query style OwnerRepository already demonstrates. What is genuinely new is caching: the two existing vet reads are @Cacheable on a cache with no eviction and no size limit, so a caller-supplied specialty must not become a key there. That decision is recorded in docs/adr/2026-09-06-specialty-filtered-vet-reads-are-not-cached.md and stated in docs/system-design.md (Contracts, Threat Model, Open Questions 5). Basis is grep plus direct file reads of the vet package and CacheConfiguration; the IDE oracle is not connected in this run, so the resolution claim rests on the weaker basis.
integration_points: VetRepository gains two specialty-filtered reads, distinct results, case folding expressed in the query; neither carries @Cacheable
VetController's two handlers gain an optional specialty request parameter and choose between the filtered and unfiltered repository read
vetList.html receives the active specialty as a model attribute and carries it on every page link
the vets cache keeps its two unfiltered entries only; CacheConfiguration is unchanged
no data binder change: the parameter is a request parameter on a String, not a field on a bound type, so the mass-assignment control in security-principles Realization is untouched

patterns.description: blank-means-broadest plus strip() on the search term, then one repository call per page; the specialty branch mirrors this shape
derived paged query on a Spring Data repository; the specialty-filtered reads follow it, adding case-insensitive matching
existing pagination model and helper; the narrowed page count comes from the filtered Page, not from a separate count

risks.risk: The specialty is concatenated into the page-link hrefs the way the numeric page is today, so caller text reaches the rendered markup unencoded
risks.mitigation: Build the narrowed page links with Thymeleaf link-expression parameters rather than the __${...}__ concatenation used for the numeric page, so the value is URL-encoded (security-principles Realization, Cross-site scripting row)

risks.risk: Case-insensitive matching is left to column type or collation, repeating the defect that makes PostgreSQL owner search case-sensitive
risks.mitigation: Express the case folding in the query itself so all three vendors match identically (system-design Known Defects, first row; Persistence section)

risks.risk: The filtered read is annotated @Cacheable("vets") by symmetry with its neighbours, letting an anonymous caller choose keys in a cache with no eviction and no size limit
risks.mitigation: Leave both filtered reads uncached (ADR 2026-09-06-specialty-filtered-vet-reads-are-not-cached); security-principles Applying this section bars a change that leaves the application weaker than the recorded baseline

risks.risk: Joining the vet-specialty association can return a veterinarian more than once if two specialty rows share a name, inflating the narrowed page count
risks.mitigation: Ask the query for distinct veterinarians (PRD REQ-VET-003: the page count reflects the narrowed list)

risks.risk: Matching logic migrates from the query into the controller, adding a fresh business rule to a web controller
risks.mitigation: The controller may normalize the parameter and choose which repository read to call; the matching stays in the query (architecture-principles Pattern Catalog, Web controller row, which the existing deviation does not extend to new rules)

risks.risk: The narrowed HTML surface reports an empty result as a failure, as owner search does when nothing matches
risks.mitigation: Render the ordinary list page with no rows and no rejection; the owner-search rejectValue branch is not the pattern to copy here (PRD REQ-VET-003 done-when: the request succeeds and the list comes back empty)

notes: docs/adr/README.md now indexes both 2026-09-06 ADRs: the product expert's non-goal ADR and the caching ADR written by this dispatch. docs/system-design.md changes: REQ-VET-003 added to five vet Contracts rows; the caching rule stated under Contracts; the stale Known Defects row on the machine-readable route retired with a pointer to the non-goal ADR; the Security Context input list, the Threat Model, and Open Question 5 updated. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit had nothing to judge. The open questions the PRD records — a visible control, several specialties at once, paging the machine-readable list — are out of scope and need no design ground until requested. The vet page size stays a local variable in the controller helper; this slice does not promote it to a constant.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Supply chain check NOT RUN — no OWASP Dependency-Check plugin is configured in build.gradle, and this reviewer has no network access, so no NVD match was performed in this pass. Resolved framework versions from build.gradle: Spring Boot 4.1.1, io.spring.dependency-management 1.1.7, spring-javaformat 0.0.48, checkstyle 12.3.1, jacoco 0.8.15, graalvm native 1.1.2, cyclonedx 3.4.1. The change adds no dependency, so this is a standing project gap rather than a defect of this slice; a human or CI should close it (the CycloneDX SBOM task already produces the input an external scanner needs).

The specialty parameter is length-unbounded before it reaches the IgnoreCase join query. Practically capped by the container's request-line limit and matched against a tiny lookup table, so the demonstrated reach does not support a finding; noted only because the same absence in a larger dataset would be a cheap scan amplifier.
approved_aspects: Data-access injection: the specialty name reaches persistence only through the Spring Data derived queries VetRepository.findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String) and (String, Pageable). Both are parameterized by construction; no query text is concatenated anywhere in the diff. Meets security-principles.md 'Injection into data access'.

XSS / output escaping: the caller-supplied specialty is never rendered as page text. It reaches the view only as a link-expression parameter (@{/vets.html(page=...,specialty=${specialty})}), which URL-encodes the value and HTML-escapes the resulting href. No th:utext, no inline JS, no remote resource, and all hrefs stay context-relative literals — no javascript:/data: URI is reachable.

Thymeleaf preprocessing removed: the four pre-existing th:href='@{'/vets.html?page=__${i}__'}' expressions were replaced with link-expression parameters. grep for '__${' across src/main/resources/templates/ now returns zero hits, so the change eliminates the last instances of the preprocessing pattern rather than extending it with request-derived text.

Cache-key poisoning / unbounded memory: the two filtered reads are deliberately not @Cacheable. Verified independently — CacheConfiguration creates the 'vets' JCache with only setStatisticsEnabled(true), and no caffeine spec or maximumSize is configured in any application*.properties, so the cache genuinely has no eviction and no size bound. Admitting a caller-chosen key there would have been a reachable unbounded-allocation DoS on an open route; the ADR and the repository Javadoc record the reason.

Boundary handling matches the neighboring implementation of the same concern: specialtyNamedBy() null/blank-checks and strips, exactly as OwnerController.processFindForm does for the lastName search parameter (OwnerController:98-103). No unjustified pattern divergence.

Exposed surface: no new endpoint. Two existing GET routes gain one optional read-only query parameter, and docs/system-design.md Security Context was updated to name it. No management-endpoint exposure changed, no state mutated, no new dependency added (build.gradle is not in the change set).

No credentials, tokens, connection strings, or other secrets appear in the diff (case-insensitive sweep for password/secret/token/api-key over the full change set returned no added lines). No logging was added, so no log-injection or secret-disclosure path.

Error handling: no new exception is constructed or caught; nothing new can carry internal detail into the error page that already renders exception messages (REQ-SYS-002 known defect). @Transactional(readOnly = true) on both new reads keeps the query at least privilege.
